comment: The checks that fail on purpose, declared once. Read by scripts/known-red.mjs (which asserts
they are STILL red and exits non-zero the day one passes), by the gated test scripts in
package.json (which exclude them from the steps that gate a merge), and by
tests/governance/known-red-gate.spec.ts (which holds all four consumers to this list).
Adding an entry here is not a way to silence a failing check. The only checks that belong are
ones whose evidence cannot be produced by an agent at all, and whose absence is itself the
record that the work is owed. Everything else red is a real failure.
Retiring an entry is not optional: the gate fails the build the moment its check passes, so
the check goes back into the suite that gates merges and a later malformed record fails again.

checks.owes: T885 (EPIC-029) — a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass, recorded as a transcript naming the reader, its version, a journey and a date
checks.why: An agent cannot hear a screen reader or see whether focus order and announcements are meaningful. A record claiming otherwise would fabricate the evidence the check exists to test for.

checks.owes: T999t (EPIC-035) — the Tier 2 defect-room journey, all seven steps: report, triage, reproduce, failing test, repair tasks, verify, close
checks.why: The journey is keyboard-only against a running application, and two of its seven steps refuse in this deployment because RepairTaskPort and TestExecution are unbound. Typing the transcript is the fabrication the check exists to test for.

checks.owes: T1992 (EPIC-047) — the Tier 2 Engineering Experts journey: open /experts, open an Expert, compare versions, open a run with its delegation tree, at 360px
checks.why: The journey needs a running application with real Experts and real runs. Every step now exists — registering, approving, registering a run with EPIC-037 and executing it in the runtime api-launcher/ composes (DEF-047-001, DEF-047-002) — but the run needs Docker, the egress network and an AI credential on a running stack, and the journey a person at the keyboard. Typing the transcript is the fabrication the check exists to test for.

checks.owes: T1301 (EPIC-038) — the Tier 2 assemble, inspect and follow-an-exclusion journey, keyboard-only against a running application, with a run-generated transcript
checks.why: POST /context/packages answers 503 in every deployment because EmbeddingPort has no owner anywhere in the programme, so the journey's first step cannot complete. Typing the transcript is the fabrication the check exists to test for.

checks.owes: T791 (EPIC-031) — run e2e/tests/epic-031-inbox.spec.ts against the reference-local stack: the Decision Inbox journey, reached in one action, approved by keyboard, the item leaving
checks.why: The run needs the reference-local stack and a seeded user's password, which an agent does not hold. The harness writes the transcript; typing one instead is the fabrication the check exists to test for.

checks.owes: T2415 (EPIC-048) — run e2e/tests/epic-048-learning.spec.ts against the reference-local stack: a candidate with five evidence items decided in the Decision Inbox and timed under two minutes (SC-LRN-007), a supersession approved narrowed at 360px, and the history read in Context → Knowledge
checks.why: The harness is authored and writes the transcript itself, but the run needs the reference-local stack and a seeded user's password, which an agent does not hold, and SC-LRN-007 is a person's decision time. Typing the transcript is the fabrication the check exists to test for.
